status_summary: Executive Order 14159 (signed 2025-01-20), section 19, paused and ordered review of federal funding agreements with nongovernmental organizations that support removable aliens, and in February 2025 FEMA clawed back more than 80 million dollars from New York City under the Shelter and Services Program, which reimburses non-federal entities for sheltering noncitizens released from DHS custody; on 2025-04-01 FEMA terminated three Pima County awards under the program; a Manhattan judge declined on 2025-03-05 to order the New York money returned immediately. Bills to end the program and rescind its balances (S. 771 and H.R. 1668) were introduced on 2025-02-27 and have had no further action. In City of Chicago et al. v. DHS, the Northern District of Illinois on 2025-11-03 enjoined eliminating the program or withholding its FY2023 and FY2024 funding on the grounds DHS gave, ruled on 2025-11-13 that the injunction is not limited to the plaintiffs, and on 2026-02-09 ordered processing of reimbursement requests submitted before termination; on 2026-05-26 the Western District of Washington set aside the termination as applied to Washington. The redirect of the money to border and detention uses was not traced.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159 (90 FR 8443) was signed; section 19 directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to review and audit funding agreements with nongovernmental organizations that serve removable or illegal aliens, halt further payments pending review, end agreements found unlawful or wasteful, keep their funding out of the agencies' appropriations requests with OMB, and start recoupment where appropriate.

S. 771 and H.R. 1668, the End FEMA Benefits for Illegal Immigrants Act, were introduced to bar FEMA from running a program that funds sheltering by non-federal entities to relieve CBP holding facilities and to rescind unobligated transferred balances; S. 771 was referred to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee and H.R. 1668 to several House committees the same day, with no later action.
A federal judge in Manhattan declined New York City's request for a temporary restraining order returning more than 80 million dollars in shelter funding that FEMA had clawed back in February 2025.

FEMA's Senior Official Performing the Duties of the Administrator issued a letter to Pima County, Arizona terminating three Shelter and Services Program grants (about 52.6 million dollars in total) with immediate effect for no longer matching DHS priorities, citing 2 CFR 200.340(a)(2), after a 2025-03-11 letter that barred new costs.
timeline.source: Pima County Board of Supervisors (copy of FEMA letter)

timeline.event: The State of Washington sued DHS and FEMA in the Western District of Washington (No. 2:25-cv-01401) over the end of its Shelter and Services Program award of about 4 million dollars.

In City of Chicago et al. v. Department of Homeland Security, No. 1:25-cv-05463 (N.D. Ill., Judge Kennelly), the court issued a memorandum opinion (Dkt. 58) granting in part the preliminary injunction sought by Chicago, Denver and Pima County, finding the freeze of Shelter and Services Program funding on the grounds in the 2025-03-11 and 2025-04-01 letters arbitrary and capricious; claims to undo past grant terminations or recover money past due were left to the Court of Federal Claims.
timeline.source: Court memorandum opinion and order (Dkt. 58), hosted by Courthouse News

timeline.event: The Northern District of Illinois entered the preliminary injunction order (Dkt. 59), enjoining DHS and FEMA from eliminating or terminating the Shelter and Services Program as created in the 2023 and 2024 DHS appropriations and from withholding FY2023 and FY2024 program funding for the reasons in the 2025-03-11 and 2025-04-01 letters, until further order.
timeline.source: Court order (Dkt. 59), hosted by the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse

timeline.event: The Northern District of Illinois denied the government's motion to clarify that the preliminary injunction covers only the three plaintiffs (Dkt. 67), holding that the court may stay the challenged agency actions under 5 U.S.C. 705 and need not limit relief to the plaintiffs.
timeline.source: Court memorandum opinion and order (Dkt. 67), hosted by the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse

timeline.event: The Northern District of Illinois granted in part the plaintiffs' motion to enforce the preliminary injunction (Dkt. 86), directing DHS and FEMA to process by 2026-02-23 all Shelter and Services Program reimbursement requests submitted before a grant was terminated, without relying on the reasons in the 2025 letters.
timeline.source: Court memorandum opinion and order (Dkt. 86), hosted by the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse

timeline.event: The Northern District of Illinois granted the plaintiffs' second motion to enforce as to reimbursement claims from non-party Shelter and Services Program grantees (Dkt. 101), with compliance due 2026-05-22, according to a case-tracking docket summary; the order itself was not opened.

Judge Rothstein granted Washington summary judgment in part on its Administrative Procedure Act claims (ECF 33) and entered judgment (ECF 34), holding the program termination policy contrary to law and arbitrary and capricious and setting it aside, with the termination of Washington's award, as applied to Washington; FEMA may not refuse to consider its reimbursement requests on the grounds held unlawful, and no payment was ordered.

title: End federal funding of NGOs that process, house or transport illegal aliens
uncertainties: No FEMA or Federal Register document on the program-wide termination was opened (a Federal Register search for the program name since 2025-01-20 returned nothing, and the FEMA program page failed to load). The February 2025 clawback is taken from news reports without a day; the 2025-04-01 termination is read from a county-hosted copy of a FEMA letter to one grantee, not a program-wide notice. The Washington ruling and judgment (ECF 33 and 34, Judge Rothstein) were read as docket summaries on a case-tracking host, whose docket excerpt was last updated 2026-07-22 and shows no notice of appeal; the orders themselves were not opened because the court docket host was inaccessible. The New York ruling comes from an AP report. The New York clawback was explained by FEMA as a gang concern at a shelter, so it may not be a general policy step. Whether FY2026 appropriations funded or rescinded the program, and whether the money was redirected to detention uses (one news item suggests so; the page could not be opened), were not checked. The 2025 DHS and FEMA grant conditions on immigration cooperation and their litigation are covered in c05-19. Independent review of 2026-10-16: the GovInfo BILLSTATUS files show both bills only introduced and referred on 2025-02-27. Update 2026-11-06: the Northern District of Illinois opinion was read from a copy hosted by Courthouse News, and the injunction order (Dkt. 59), the ruling denying the motion to limit it to the plaintiffs (Dkt. 67) and the first enforcement order (Dkt. 86) from court copies hosted by the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse; the second enforcement order of 2026-05-08 rests only on the docket summary on that host, whose latest entry is dated 2026-05-11 and shows no appeal (a letter from a U.S. senator of 2026-07-13 on senate.gov dates that order 2026-05-07), and whether DHS complied with the 2026-05-22 deadline is not known (a Senate letter of 2026-07-13 asks for a status report). The stage moves to blocked because the injunction reaches the program as a whole, not only the plaintiffs, and the bills have not moved; the injunction covers only FY2023 and FY2024 program funding, does not reach other nongovernmental funding paused under Executive Order 14159, and leaves past terminations to the Court of Federal Claims, so progress earned is kept at 35. Whether DHS has complied with the enforcement orders and whether later fiscal years funded the program were not established. A search found a trade report of 2026-05-14 that the administration dropped appeals of rulings on FEMA grant immigration-cooperation conditions, which concern c05-19 and not this program. No new activity on S. 771 or H.R. 1668 (BILLSTATUS shows introduction and referral only) and no Federal Register document on the program since 2025-01-20 was found.
